text:
marta: quick heads-up — noticed a p95 latency bump on cache-heavy traffic during the midnight rollout window, looks related to batching heuristics
kevin: can you paste the numbers? which metric spiked?
marta: p95 generation latency up ~220ms -> +1200ms in one slot, throughput unchanged. kernel_launch_rate from profiler jumped ~3x for the affected kernel. trace attached in perf logs.
lia: interesting — are these mostly prefix-cache hits? any change in avg seq length?
marta: yes, >80% prefix hits for that workload. avg request token_count 48 but cached_prefix_len ~32 on many requests, so effective new tokens are ~16.
sam: that rings a bell. our current packer uses "virtual length" = total tokens for admission and kernel selection, so cache-hit-heavy requests look long and get packed as single-request microbatches. that increases kernel launches per real token.
kevin: ugh. kernel selection then picks the large-sequence kernel which has worse per-token startup for these small new-token cases. perf regression plausible.
lia: can we compute effective_tokens = max(1, total - cached_prefix) and use that for admission? simple change, but need to check interactions with prefix-affinity packing and KV cache re-use.
marta: I prototyped a quick change on dev-rt: set effective_vlen = max(1, seq_len - prefix_cache_len) and feed that to packer. microbatch size bumped ~2.5x and kernel_launch_rate dropped similarly. p95 back to baseline.
infra-bot: deploy succeeded: batcher-proto/ae3d -> canary (10%)
kevin: nice. any downside? under heavy cache-duplication we might overpack and increase memory pressure for KV caches?
sam: two concerns: (1) fairness — customers with big uncached prompts shouldn't be starved if we bias packing to combine cache-hits with each other; (2) we need to ensure kernel selection still considers absolute seq_len for kernel that uses workspace memory.
lia: proposal: add two tunables — cache_hit_vlen_scale (float) and min_effective_batch_fill (tokens). Default scale=1.0 (no change). If >0, effective_vlen = max(1, seq_len - cache_hit_vlen_scale * prefix_cache_len). Also add admissions policy that tries to co-locate cache-hit requests with non-hits when it helps reach token budget, but doesn't evict existing queued non-hits below priority threshold.
marta: also we saw one case where prefix cache fragmentation caused KV lookups to miss at runtime after packing because we changed order; need to preserve per-request KV affinity when reordering. kept in prototype via stable-grouping by prefix-id.
kevin: can we simulate on loadtester? any reproducible harness?
marta: yes — run: 
```
./tools/loadgen --scenario=prefix-heavy --qps=300 --avg-tokens=48 --prefix-hit-ratio=0.85 --seed=42
```
collect perf via /tools/trace-collect --tag=cache_vlen_test
sam: let's add a small perf counter: kernel_launches_per_real_token and serviced_effective_batch_fill to telemetry. graphs will show improvement.
nora: if we change kernel selection inputs, add a safety-gate: only use effective_vlen for packer admission and keep kernel selection to consider both total_seq_len and effective_vlen with a heuristic rule. i.e. pick kernel that supports total_seq_len but prefer kernels optimized for small real-token counts.
lia: agree. we should stage in three steps: (1) telemetry + loadgen baseline (2) enable effective_vlen in packer only, canary 10% (3) enable kernel selection hint + A/B 50%/50% after 24h.
kevin: assignable tasks?
marta: i can do (1) and the loadtest reproducer. kevin can wire the telemetry counters. lia can implement the packer change and the new tunables. sam will draft the canary playbook and memory pressure checks. nora will review kernel selection safety gate.
kevin: timeline?
lia: aim for PRs by EOD tomorrow, canary rollout Thursday if tests pass.
kevin: sounds good. one more note — watch for billing/accounting: effective token accounting might change cost attribution slightly for cached prefixes. sync with billing before full rollout.
marta: thanks — I'll post perf plots when I have them. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks, team.
